verdict: PARTLY REFUTED BY A FOLLOW-UP TEST — corrected here rather than left standing. WHAT STANDS (measured): cpfind's raw control points DO reach the corner (rho_max 1.60-1.78 vs a corner at 1.80) and cpclean removes almost all of them (9.9%->0.0% beyond rho 1.50 on july31/set-01); and the destructive half is cpclean STEP 2 (whole-panorama), not step 1 — MEASURED by running each step alone on aug06/set-01's raw set: step 1 removes ONE point of 225 and keeps corner support (max 1.77, 5.6% beyond 1.5), step 2 alone reproduces the shipped result exactly (180, max 1.61, 1.9%). WHAT IS REFUTED: the MECHANISM I attributed it to — 'step 2 deletes corner points because a,b,c are not yet fitted'. Discriminating test: seed step 2 with a project that already carries a FITTED a,b,c (pto_template) and skip re-optimisation (cpclean -w -s). It removes the same population: 219 -> 183, rho_max 1.77 -> 1.65, 5.9% -> 2.7% beyond 1.5 — indistinguishable from the model-free prune. So the corner points have large residuals under ANY model: they are predominantly BAD MATCHES (cpfind SIFT on aberrated, low-SNR corner stars), not good constraints being wrongly discarded. The -n threshold is also exhausted: both-steps at n=3,4,5,6,8 all return the identical 178 points, so the removed population sits far beyond mean+8sigma. CONSEQUENCE: corner support cannot be won by reordering or relaxing the prune. It needs corner CORRESPONDENCES that are actually good — a detection/matching problem, not a pruning one.
verdict_superseded: DETECTION IS NOT THE PROBLEM — THE PRUNE IS. cpfind's raw control points DO reach the corner (rho_max 1.60-1.78 against a corner at 1.80; july31/set-01 puts 9.9% of its CPs beyond rho 1.5). The strict cpclean then removes essentially all of them: 9.9% -> 0.0% (july31), 4.5% -> 0.4% (set-02), 1.0% -> 0.0% (set-03), with rho_max falling 1.76->1.24, 1.78->1.50, 1.60->1.47. MECHANISM: cpclean prunes on residuals against the CURRENT model, and the staged optimise runs ROTATIONS ONLY before the prune — so the residual it judges comes from a model with NO distortion terms, and an unmodelled radial distortion's residual GROWS WITH RADIUS. The prune therefore deletes the largest-radius points systematically: the control points that would constrain the corner are removed BECAUSE the corner is not yet modelled. Self-defeating loop. COROLLARY, and it corrects a standing record: july31/set-01's refit was rejected as 'CP coverage radially BANDED, fit untrustworthy'. The banding was CREATED by this prune — its raw coverage was the BEST of any fit measured here. The rejection's conclusion (do not ship that fit) stands; its stated cause does not. CONSEQUENCE: the corner-true refit needs no new detection and no new frames — it needs the prune to run AFTER a,b,c are fitted, so corner points are judged against a model that can represent them.

verdict: REFUTED AS INVOKED — and the refutation is informative. Siril 1.4.4 CAN solve this class natively (MEASURED: seqplatesolve -order=3, 2/2 members solved, 388 and 371 matched stars, residual sigx/sigy 0.96/0.85 and 0.99/0.93 px, centres agreeing with astrometry.net to 0.001 deg, RA---TAN-SIP + A_ORDER 3 written into each member's own header). But `register -disto=` is a SHARED-SOLUTION facility, not per-image reprojection:   arm (each member undistorted by ITS OWN SIP, then composed) 3.99 / 6.42 / 6.19 px (centre/mid/outer) against the shipped lensfun control's 0.29 / 0.63 / 2.10 / 2.99 — WORSE, and worst at the CENTRE, which no distortion story explains. MECHANISM, isolated by a further one-knob probe: warping a SINGLE member by its OWN solution and composing it against its own unwarped self gives 8.50 / 9.45 / 6.76 px. The polynomial is not identity-preserving on its own — it only cancels when EVERY member shares the same solution, which is exactly Siril's documented use (`distortion terms from a previous platesolve solution`, applied to a sequence). Siril's own design therefore assumes ONE optical state per sequence — the same one-model-per-combine-family pattern, now confirmed as the tool's assumption rather than this repo's invention. SCOPE: this refutes the INVOCATION, not the architecture. The industry-standard operation is resampling each exposure onto a COMMON output WCS using its own full solution (CD matrix AND distortion), which is SWarp's model; Siril has no such command, and neither SWarp nor python `reproject` is installed here (SWarp is packaged for this distro at 2.41.5-3). ALSO RETIRED: the standing belief that Siril's internal solver cannot handle this class. It cannot handle single ULTRA-WIDE TRAILED frames — the measurement that established it — but STACKED members have round stars and solve fine. The belief had silently widened past its evidence.

question: Is Nikon's embedded per-shot distortion model the per-OPTICAL-STATE source that would replace the in-house hugin fit? TOOLS.md had recorded the coefficients as present-but-unpriced.
instrument: exiftool 13.55, headers only, one invocation over the whole archive: -r -ext NEF -csv -n over sessions/ (n=7702 frames; july14/july23/july31/aug06; 19 light sets + 4 dark sets), reading Nikon DistortionInfo (MakerNote tag 0x0005) RadialDistortionCoefficient1..3 plus PowerUpTime, LensPositionAbsolute, FocalLength, VignetteCoefficient1..3. Cross-checked against exiv2, LibRaw 0.22.1, dcraw; darktable 5.4.1 maker coverage read from src/common/image.h and confirmed against the installed binaries.
verdict: STATIC, NOT PER-STATE - the route does not replace the fit. MEASURED: exactly TWO distinct coefficient triples exist in 7702 frames. A=(0.01821231842,-0.01132106781,0.05938911438) covers 7355 frames including EVERY light set of all four nights; B=(0.01828289032,-0.01136207581,0.05913734436) appears in july31/darks only (347 frames). THE KILL: the july31 and aug06 members measured 4.07 px apart at the corner (cross_night_state_difference) carry BYTE-IDENTICAL coefficients, so adopting this model for both nights IS adopting a shared model and reproduces that failure by construction.
mechanism: The block latches per POWER-UP, not per optical state. Grouped by Nikon:PowerUpTime, 14 of 15 power-up cycles across four nights emit triple A; one emits B, and the VignetteInfo coefficients flip in that same power-up (VignetteCoefficient1 -4.667527199 -> -4.62051487), so the whole correction block is re-latched together. LensPositionAbsolute - the state field that DOES move - does not predict the coefficients: it spans -17..0, takes the value 0 in BOTH groups, and july31/set-01 holds 3 distinct lens positions under ONE triple. The corner difference between the two triples is order-independent (at rho=1 every term multiplies by 1) and equals the sum of the coefficient deltas: 2.222061e-04 * 3634.40 = 0.808 px, i.e. the model's ENTIRE range of motion over four nights is one fifth of the defect it would have to explain.
application_gap: MEASURED, and it is the harder blocker. DECODE: exiftool alone. exiv2 returns only Nikon3.VignetteControl, LibRaw 0.22.1 has zero 'distort' strings, dcraw reports nothing - and darktable/RawTherapee read maker notes THROUGH exiv2. APPLY: darktable's dt_image_correction_type_t enum is {NONE,SONY,FUJI,DNG,OLYMPUS,PANASONIC} with no NIKON, and RawTherapee PR#7100 (merged 5.11) implements the identical maker set - two independent projects at the same boundary. The installed darktable 5.4.1 carries DT_IOP_LENS_METHOD_EMBEDDED_METADATA and WarpRectilinear but cannot reach a Nikon NEF. Only live route is DNG opcodes, and the sole converter that writes them (Adobe DNG Converter) is proprietary and Windows/macOS-only (Wine-runnable); the free native one (dnglab) explicitly drops lens opcodes.
model_form: DOC (Adobe dng_sdk dng_lens_correction.h): WarpRectilinear radial w(r)=kr0*r+kr1*r^3+kr2*r^5+kr3*r^7, with r=1.0 anchored at the farthest corner of the active area and an invertibility constraint over that domain - so a manufacturer model is corner-defined BY CONSTRUCTION, which is exactly what the hugin fits cannot reach at rho=1.80. Nikon stores three rationals with denominator 2^20 at block offsets 0x14/0x1c/0x24; a FOURTH 2^20 rational at +0x40 that exiftool does not decode co-varies with them (74572/2^20=0.0711174 vs 74330/2^20=0.0708866) - plausibly the autoscale factor, unsettled. That Nikon's triple IS DNG's kr1..kr3 is UNVERIFIED COMMUNITY; the pixls.us reverse-engineering effort (t/36733) has derived no formula and no code, and names the exiv2 gap as its own blocker. NORMALISATION settled by arithmetic, not by document: under half-diagonal (rho=1 at corner) the model gives +6.6% corner stretch; under the repo's half-short-side convention the same coefficients give +197.8%, which is not a lens.
null_result: The on-rig attempt to MEASURE the model empirically is a CLEAN NULL. Design: every NEF embeds a full-size 6048x4032 in-camera JPEG with the correction applied, so its displacement field against a darktable 'nodist' render of the same NEF is the applied model. Executed with sep 1.4.1 and three matchers (polar-angle, centre-out bootstrap, patch phase-correlation). No correspondence exists to fit: the central translation vote, which must peak sharply since the warp is ~0 at the centre, gave 11 votes against a 99.9pct of 7 at every threshold from 4 to 50 sigma. MECHANISM, identified by direct inspection of matched 400x400 centre patches: the in-camera JPEG is dominated by 8x8 JPEG block artifacts, not stars - a 2.5 s ISO 1600 sub at 70 mm is sky-noise-dominated and the lossy 8-bit encode destroys the faint star field. This is a data limit, not a method limit, and it is the SAME limit that starved the hugin corner fit. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: one frame from this body+lens at this focal length on a bright structured subject (daylight or moonlit landscape), where the in-camera JPEG carries real detail. Two minutes at the next acquisition; converts the model form from COMMUNITY to MEASURED.
scope: All 7702 frames are at 70 mm, so this measures 'static across nights, sets, focus positions and power-ups AT ONE FOCAL LENGTH'. A zoom-indexed table is untested here and near-certain to exist; a dataset at another zoom setting would get a different, equally static triple.
consequences: F2 is untouched - corner-support starvation and ~3 px fit reproducibility (75340bb) still gate multi-night combining, and the T-1 trade options (a)/(b)/(c) stand exactly as costed. What is bought: TOOLS.md's unpriced entry can be closed, and no future session need re-open it hoping the coefficients are per-shot. What survives: the embedded model as a candidate STATIC base model that reaches the corner - the one place the community lensfun profile measurably fails (paraxial centre band, july14 centre 5.30 vs perpendicular 3.60 px).
next_test_if_wanted: E0 GATE, cheap and decisive: convert ONE NEF with Adobe DNG Converter under Wine, read exiftool -v3 -OpcodeList3, compare WarpRectilinear kr0..kr3 against the MakerNote triple. PASS proves route (b) end-to-end AND hands route (c) the model form and normalisation that no public source has published. FAIL closes both routes for the cost of one file. Pre-registered: E0 PASS required before any pixel is warped by this model. E2 then has its answer pre-registered - both nights share coefficients, so a cross-night compose under this model should reproduce ~4.07 px, and landing at the 0.14-0.35 px floor instead would REFUTE the reading that 4.07 px is a physical state difference.

hypothesis: PRE-STATED after the owner's field correction that the generic (one-for-everything) model DID combine sets, cross-set and cross-night successfully: re-measure the load-bearing `cross_night_state_difference` cell independently, because it is the single number behind 'a shared model does not cross nights' and it was not measured by this session.
instrument: scripts/qa/member_separation.py (validated on six same-night cells against the owner's own eye verdicts), on freshly registered pairs; plus a bootstrap and a tail check on the raw per-star separations
verdict:
TWO findings, and the second limits the first.
1. THE ONE-KNOB COMPARISON IS ROBUST AND SUPPORTS THE OWNER. Same two nights, same member pair, only the model differing: ONE shared model beats TWO per-set models at EVERY zone — centre 0.41 vs 0.92, mid 1.09 vs 1.31, outer 2.07 vs 2.73, corner 3.38 vs 5.34 (rho>=0.70 binning). A single generic model is measurably the better cross-night configuration, which is what the owner's field experience says.
2. THE INSTRUMENT IS NOT VALIDATED FOR LARGE RE-AIM GEOMETRY, so no ABSOLUTE cross-night number from it should be trusted — including the 4.07 px that has been driving this arc. Its zones are CANVAS-radial, which equals FIELD-radial only when the members are near co-pointed (true for every cell it was validated on: 98-500 px offsets). Across a re-aim the canvas centre lies between two optical axes, so a canvas corner is at a different field radius in each member. Symptoms, measured: the profile goes NON-MONOTONIC (outer 2.07 worse than corner 0.71), the corner median swings 0.71 -> 3.38 on a 0.10 change of the zone bound, the distribution is heavy-tailed (median 0.71, p75 5.21, p90 5.92) and the bootstrap band is 0.55-3.89. My centre/mid/outer reproduce the prior session's X1 closely (0.41/1.09/2.07 vs 0.33/0.99/1.87); only the corner diverges, which is exactly the zone the geometry breaks.
CONSEQUENCE: `cross_night_state_difference`'s 4.07 px is DOWNGRADED from a measured fact to an instrument-limited estimate, and every conclusion resting on it — 'a shared family model does not cross nights', F1 demoted to same-night-only, F2 promoted as the multi-night requirement — loses its evidence. It is not refuted either; it is UNMEASURED. The fix is to bin by each member's OWN field radius via its own WCS rather than by canvas radius, and to re-run the cross-night cells on that.

verdict:
MEASURED: set-01's elevation DOES NOT EXIST IN ITS DATA. Every one of its five 100-frame groups reads 0.40-0.45 px off-axis under the pinned model — indistinguishable from set-02's groups (0.45-0.46) and BETTER than them on truncated-mean FWHM (2.74-2.79 vs 2.82-2.84). The 0.82 px appears only in the 500-frame full-set product, i.e. it is CREATED AT THE GROUP->SET COMPOSE. Set-02 is the built-in depth control: it spans the same 100->500 frame increase and grows only +0.11 (0.46 -> 0.57) where set-01 grows +0.39 (0.43 -> 0.82), so stack depth alone does not account for it.
CONSEQUENCE — this is the founding evidence of the whole per-set optical-state arc. `BACKLOG:optical-state-models` opens with 'The july-fitted pinned model measured against aug06: ... off-axis 0.82 vs 0.16-0.47 ... the field-dependent signature of a state change'. It is not a state change: it is a compose artifact of the SAME class as the defect this whole investigation chased. The doctrine `the lens model keys on the OPTICAL STATE, per set` (9095564) generalised from one number that was never about optics, and the adoption A/B (dd38019) then read 1 WIN / 3 NULL and adopted per-set granularity for all four sets — giving new models to three sets that measured no benefit, which is exactly the heterogeneity that broke the cross-set and cross-night combine (2.99 px / 5.34 px corner disagreement).
The per-set optical-state doctrine is REFUTED at its root. Note what is NOT refuted: fitting a model from a set's own frames (the july14 method) — that produced the model every accepted combine used.

BOTH ARMS ANSWER, AND THEY ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS.
1. REGISTRATION SCOPE IS WORTH 6.5x ON MEMBER DISAGREEMENT, one knob, identical frames: per-group auto references give a worst pair of 3.12 px, one global reference gives 0.48 px. THE CHANGE IS PHYSICAL, TIME-PROGRESSIVE AND ONE-SIDED. armB's blur readout was confounded (its auto reference landed at frame 6, so late blocks were also the most distant). armC pins the reference to frame 125 and separates them: at MATCHED drift distance the LATE block is worse than its early twin by +0.25 px / -0.064 roundness (99f vs 101f) and +0.27 px / -0.104 (49f vs 51f), on the LEFT field only. verdict:
THE ASYMMETRY IS REAL AND THE ELEMENT WORKS; THE STANDALONE KNOB IS A LOSS.
(1) The lens's DISPLACEMENT field carries a large decentring term. A centred radial model of ANY degree leaves 6.7-8.5 px RMS on a raw frame; two extra Brown tangential parameters halve it to 3.0-4.8 px, and a free distortion centre reaches the same residual with a centre offset of ~180-210 px in x and ~210-240 px in y. Both parameterisations reproduce across three frames, two nights and different pointings. The residual a centred radial model cannot fit is EVEN in x, which is exactly what a radial basis error cannot produce.
(2) lensfun 0.3.4 CAN apply a displaced distortion centre: <center x= y=/> is parsed by database.cpp and applied by mod-coord.cpp, the installed .so carries the string, and darktable's output changes when it is present. The unit is half the image height (2020 px), matching the independently probed radius normalisation.
(3) Installing it on top of the pinned a,b,c is a LOSS at every sign: 2.589 px -> 4.235-7.610 px. That is not a sign error, it is the coupling — a,b,c are fitted ABOUT a centre. A ~285 px centre shift perturbs the correction by ~20 px while the residual it must remove is 2.6 px RMS, so a centre small enough not to hurt is too small to represent the measured decentring.
(4) HUGIN CANNOT SUPPLY THE CENTRE EITHER. The fit script's d,e stage is degenerate in 4 of 5 preserved fits: aug06/set-02 d=6.3e6 e=-4.5e7 with a=282 b=1120 c=4733; july31/set-01 d=5.6e6 e=-1.4e7 with a=361 b=422 c=496; aug06/set-01 d=-177 e=+378 on an already-degenerate abc; aug06/set-03 d=-122 e=-524. Only aug06/set-00 stays bounded (d=+1.8 e=+24.0), and it disagrees with the absolute measurement by an order of magnitude. Mechanism: Hugin fits d,e jointly with per-image y,p,r on BETWEEN-FRAME correspondences, where a centre shift is nearly degenerate with per-image yaw/pitch. The absolute-catalogue fit has ONE global affine instead, so the centre is identifiable there and not here.

verdict:
THE ONE-SIDED TERM IS RADIAL ELONGATION WITH AN ASYMMETRIC AMPLITUDE — a field aberration of the coma family, in the optics, and it is NOT any of the things previously suspected.
ELIMINATED, each by measurement here: (1) a DETECTION/BRIGHTNESS artefact — the gradient survives inside amplitude quartiles in 6/6 sets, though median brightness varies 2-10x across x; (2) PURE DEFOCUS, i.e. sensor tilt as a focus-plane tilt — that inflates BOTH axes on the soft side, and the MINOR axis is measured symmetric left-vs-right while the major is not; (3) RESIDUAL MOTION / in-exposure trailing — that is a fixed direction in sensor coordinates, and phi tracks the field azimuth instead; (4) RESIDUAL DISTORTION — the geometry fits a centred ptlens model to a 0.27 px median (ledger ptlens_joint_refit_free_centre).
CONSISTENT WITH the centred distortion: distortion and coma respond differently to a decentred or tilted element, so a lens can have well-centred distortion and an off-centre aberration field. The two measurements do not conflict.
INFERRED (labelled): radial flare growing with field radius, amplitude larger on one side, is the signature of coma with a decentred aberration field. Astigmatism is disfavoured because it flips radial-to-tangential across best focus and we measure RADIAL on BOTH sides; field curvature is disfavoured because it is isotropic defocus.
what_is_NOT_settled: Whether the asymmetry originates in the lens (element decentre/tilt) or in the body (sensor not orthogonal) — this data cannot separate them, and a focus bracket would (the sharp zone sweeps across the frame as focus changes if the plane is tilted). Nor is the magnitude of the residual FIXED-direction component separated from the radial one at the frame centre, where both statistics are unordered.
consequences: It is optics, so no distortion model of any expressiveness removes it, and no re-registration does either. What CAN address it: spatially-varying deconvolution (RC-Astro BXT is designed for exactly this and is a deliberate uninstalled gap; Cosmic Clarity is installed, exposes --auto_detect_psf 'measure PSF per chunk', and its field behaviour is unprobed); PSF homogenisation before stacking (the DES/Pan-STARRS answer, docs/untracked-widefield-standards.md 4.4); down-weighting the affected zone. PLACEMENT IS NOT FREE: the PSF is fixed in SENSOR coordinates and the sky drifts ~1000 px across the sensor, so after registration every output position holds a blend of a dozen different sensor-position PSFs and there is no well-defined PSF left to correct. Any such stage belongs PER FRAME, IN SENSOR SPACE — after debayer (a CFA mosaic cannot be deconvolved), before the undistort warp (whose interpolation adds its own position-dependent blur), and unambiguously before register.

CORRECTION_the_exponent_reference_was_wr.what_was_claimed: 'the measured radial exponent is 2.1-3.8, never near 1, so this is NOT the coma family' — comparing a measured ELLIPTICITY exponent against coma's BLUR exponent.
CORRECTION_the_exponent_reference_was_wr.why_it_is_wrong: Seidel gives the BLUR SIZE: coma grows linearly with field height, astigmatism quadratically. Ellipticity is not a blur size. Blurs convolve, so variances add: a^2 = w^2 + k*l^2, hence a^2 - b^2 = k*l^2 and e = (a^2-b^2)/(a^2+b^2) ~ k*l^2/(2w^2). BOTH the ellipticity and the second-moment difference go as l^2, so the reference exponents against field radius are 2 for coma and 4 for astigmatism, NOT 1 and 2.
CORRECTION_the_exponent_reference_was_wr.the_corrected_reading: measured ellipticity exponents 2.09-3.80 per set (1.12-2.81 on the unnormalised second-moment difference) are BLUR exponents of 0.56-1.90, clustering near 1. CORRECTION_the_exponent_reference_was_wr.caught_by: the parallel audit session, which asked why the record's second estimator column (exponent_unnormalised, 1.115 on aug06/set-02) was not reported alongside the first. answering_the_two_estimator_question_dir.which_is_principled: NEITHER is more principled for naming the family, because both scale as l^2 and therefore carry the SAME reference exponents. They differ only in whether the slowly-growing denominator a^2+b^2 is divided out. The ratio form is the better-CONDITIONED of the two here (R2 0.40-0.97 against 0.38-0.88, and two sets return no usable unnormalised fit at all) because dividing by a^2+b^2 removes the star-to-star size scatter that dominates the raw difference. That is a variance argument, not a physics one, and it does not license quoting one column and suppressing the other.

CONSUMER_1_theta0_vs_drift_bearing.why_it_is_the_discriminator: the trail points along the sky's apparent motion, whose direction in the sensor frame rotates as the field is carried across the sky. A sensor-fixed cause (demosaic/CFA anisotropy, sensor tilt, an astigmatism aligned to the sensor axes) does not rotate. theta0 comes from star SHAPES; the drift bearing comes from star POSITIONS between two frames on a ~30 s baseline against the 2.5 s trail, so the bearing is far better determined than the trail it is being compared to.
CONSUMER_1_theta0_vs_drift_bearing.instrument: Siril findstar per frame; cross-match between frames k and k+10 gives the displacement field, whose bearing IS the drift direction. CONSUMER_1_theta0_vs_drift_bearing.sampling: 10 blocks at frames 1, 51, 101, ..., 451; each block is the pair (k, k+10), giving one bearing and one theta0 per block across the full 1497 s.
CONSUMER_1_theta0_vs_drift_bearing.PREDICTS_IF_TRAILING: theta0 tracks the bearing frame by frame: the offset (theta0 - bearing) is CONSTANT and near 0 mod 180, and the slope of theta0 against bearing across the 10 blocks is 1.
CONSUMER_1_theta0_vs_drift_bearing.PREDICTS_IF_SENSOR_FIXED: theta0 is constant while the bearing rotates: slope 0.
CONSUMER_1_theta0_vs_drift_bearing.WHAT_A_NULL_LOOKS_LIKE_AND_IT_IS_A_REAL_: if theta0 does NOT track the bearing, that is a positive finding about the fixed term — it is sensor-fixed, not trailing — and it must be reported as such rather than as a failed build. CONSUMER_2_latitude_and_LST_recovery.question: can the corpus recover the observing site itself, closing the OWNER-SUPPLIED, TRANSCRIBED, UNVERIFIED provenance on scripts/setup/site.json?
CONSUMER_2_latitude_and_LST_recovery.mechanism: on a fixed (non-rotating) tripod the camera is static and the sky turns, so the angle between the sensor axes and celestial north IS the parallactic angle q. Per-frame plate solves give q(t) from each CD matrix. tan q = sin(HA) / (tan(lat) cos(dec) - sin(dec) cos(HA)), with HA = LST - RA, so q(t) at several times within one set constrains (lat, LST) jointly — time is known, so the HA advance across the set is known and only the zero point is free.

Either is a REAL result: report the constraint region rather than a point estimate, state that one set has no lever, and name what would (more pointings, a longer baseline). Reporting a latitude whose error bar is not measured would be the failure mode here.

A_TOOL_FACT_THAT_BOUNDS_THIS_WHOLE_COMPA: PSFEx exposes NO position-resolved shape in any output. Its XML reports min/mean/max of FWHM, ellipticity, e1 and e2 over the NSNAP grid, and the .psf carries model coefficients. So a position-resolved head-to-head CANNOT avoid re-deriving a shape from the model — the thing the repo's own rule warns against — and the re-derived shape is estimator-dependent by construction. PSFEx's own figures come from a MOFFAT FIT (the XML carries MoffatBeta); this reconstruction uses adaptive moments. Those are different estimators and are not expected to agree on a profile that is neither Gaussian nor Moffat, which is exactly what a trailed star is (psf_calib.json).

b_node_count_third.why_it_is_a_discriminator_we_thought_did: Nodal Aberration Theory (Thompson 2005 JOSA A; Schechter & Levinson 2011 arXiv:1009.0708): a decentred or tilted element leaves coma UNINODAL — one zero, displaced — while astigmatism becomes BINODAL, the single zero splitting in two. Node COUNT is topological, works at a single focus, needs no bracket and no sign flip.
b_node_count_third.test: map the spin-2 field over (x,y) and count its zeros. One => coma family. Two => astigmatism, and the placement then separates misalignment from figure error.

WHY_THE_SPLIT_IS_STILL_NOT_A_RESULT.THE_ALGEBRAIC_DEGENERACY_WHICH_IS_THE_RE: a term along -u(bearing) is IDENTICAL in form to having over-estimated the trail amplitude, since R = (t_true - t)*u(b) + S. So the fitted drift-perp amplitude of 0.08078 is EITHER a genuine physical term anti-parallel to the drift, OR the amount by which the trail prediction is too large. Those are the same vector. No amount of additional data separates them, because the degeneracy is in the model and not in the sample.

That was wrong: it assumed the ONLY thing along u(b) is a trail-amplitude error. A genuine physical term anti-parallel to the drift is equally consistent with the same fit and contradicts nothing. The two readings are degenerate, which is the finding.

So the residual is not purely a demosaic or readout term, and the CFA-undebayered follow-up that would have tested that is not justified by this result.

Both are acquisition changes. THE DATA IS A GIVEN, so neither is available.

method: three FULL-SENSOR 6064x4040 frames with sub-pixel shifts, each pushed through darktable --style lensdist, then the three warped frames registered and resampled by Siril in ACTUAL SERIES (register -2pass -transf=homography, seqapplyreg -interp=lanczos4). The earlier separate arm happened to pick image 5, which is why it did not surface there. Measure a NON-REFERENCE frame, always, or the instrument reads zero for the wrong reason.

PROBE_ii_are_there_OTF_ZEROS_inside_the_.why_it_decides_something: information at an OTF zero is destroyed and no deconvolution returns it. A zero would bound what ANY restoration can recover, and it would do so without needing the coma-vs-astigmatism label settled.
PROBE_ii_are_there_OTF_ZEROS_inside_the_.method: 2-D FFT of the PSFEx field model's PSF at the frame centre and at two corners, normalised, examined inside |f| <= 0.5 cycles per IMAGE pixel. The stamp is oversampled 2.05x (PSF_SAMP 0.4876), so the image Nyquist sits well inside the stamp's own band.
PROBE_ii_are_there_OTF_ZEROS_inside_the_.A_FIRST_PASS_OF_MINE_WAS_WRONG_AND_IS_RE: the first test asked only whether the minimum in-band MTF fell below a threshold; it read 0.004-0.009 and printed 'IN-BAND NULL PRESENT'. That conflates a monotone ROLL-OFF to near-zero at the band edge — which EVERY PSF does, and which bounds SNR rather than information — with a true NULL, an interior minimum the MTF recovers from. The distinction is the entire point of the probe.
PROBE_ii_are_there_OTF_ZEROS_inside_the_.the_correct_test: along 12 radial cuts per field position, does the MTF ever RECOVER after its running minimum? An interior null recovers; a roll-off does not.

MEASURED.corner_BR: 1 of 12 at 0.0223, i.e. at the noise level of the model

PROBE_ii_are_there_OTF_ZEROS_inside_the_.verdict: NO IN-BAND OTF ZERO at any field position. The corner is ATTENUATED, not nulled. Restoration is therefore SNR-bounded, not information-bounded.
PROBE_ii_are_there_OTF_ZEROS_inside_the_.the_quantitative_part_which_is_the_usefu: radial MTF, median over azimuth, centre against corners: at |f| = 0.1 cyc/px 0.837 / 0.685 / 0.724; at 0.2, 0.575 / 0.317 / 0.397; at 0.3, 0.265 / 0.079 / 0.149; at 0.4, 0.072 / 0.028 / 0.043. So the corner runs roughly 3x down on the centre through the mid band, and any restoration that flattens that must apply ~3x gain at 0.3 cyc/px — amplifying noise by the same factor. THAT is the recoverability ceiling, and it is a noise budget rather than a hard wall.
PROBE_ii_are_there_OTF_ZEROS_inside_the_.THE_CAVEAT_THAT_LIMITS_THIS: this is the OTF of the PSFEx MODEL, not of the true PSF. The model's eigen-PSFs are full 25x25 images and CAN represent a null, so the polynomial field fit is not the obstacle — but PSFEx fits to real, noisy, undersampled stars, and a sharp null could be smoothed away by that fit. The probe therefore shows no MODELLED null; it cannot prove no TRUE null. Settling that needs a null-sensitive measurement on the stars themselves, which is not done.

verdict: (i) drizzle REFUSES debayered RGB, measured. (ii) no in-band OTF zero in the modelled PSF, so the corner is attenuation not destruction, and the ceiling is a ~3x noise-gain budget at 0.3 cyc/px rather than a wall.

THE_CONFOUND_THAT_GATES_EVERYTHING.what: july27's findstar detection list is heavily contaminated with NON-STELLAR detections, and aug06's is not.

The mean/median ratio of a^2-b^2 is 27.7 on july27 against 1.1 on aug06, so ANY statistic built on means — which every spin-2 fit is — is tail-dominated on july27 and not on aug06.
THE_CONFOUND_THAT_GATES_EVERYTHING.what_it_did_to_the_first_fit: the unnormalised field-constant term came out at 25.81 px^2 against a median a^2-b^2 of 7.61, with the radial term at 0.1-0.5 SE (i.e. unmeasured). Those numbers are artefacts of the tail, not measurements.
THE_CONFOUND_THAT_GATES_EVERYTHING.why_it_is_EXPOSURE_DEPENDENT_and_therefo: longer exposures at longer cadence catch more and longer satellite/aircraft trails per frame. So the contamination itself scales with exposure — which is exactly the axis the test reads. A trail-amplitude scaling test cannot be run on populations whose contamination also scales with exposure.
